extracted.intended_audience: electric cooperative leaders, policymakers, regulators, and stakeholders concerned with grid reliability and energy transition
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries of policy positions, recommendations, and practical measures electric cooperatives and their advocates present to lawmakers and regulators to preserve grid reliability and affordability while managing the energy transition. Focuses on financing, permitting, generation mix, resilience, and consumer protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain exceptional reliability and affordability
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and industry actions must maintain the exceptional reliability and affordability that American families and businesses expect and deserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work constructively with industry to achieve emissions/reliability goals without sacrificing affordable, 24/7 service to consumers; weigh reliability impacts and costs when considering policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy transition timelines must be realistic and technology-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: The ongoing energy transition must recognize the need for time and technology and be inclusive of all energy sources to maintain reliability and affordability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mandates that transform the energy sector on unreasonable or unrealistic timelines; account for regional differences in resource availability and the potential for stranded assets; ensure required technologies and transmission upgrades exist before rapid retirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive all-of-the-above generation portfolios
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain diversified 'all options' generation portfolios that include renewables as well as conventional thermal dispatchable generation to provide service and pricing flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributed and intermittent resources should be complemented by dispatchable/baseload generation to meet 24/7 demand and avoid reliability shortfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain dispatchable/baseload generation capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure there is sufficient baseload/dispatchable generation available to meet continuous demand and back up intermittent renewables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investments such as efficient reciprocating natural gas engines can complement wind and solar; policies should not force premature retirement of dispatchable resources essential for reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level playing field for co-ops via direct-pay tax incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Because not-for-profit electric cooperatives do not pay federal income taxes, they are ineligible for tax-credit structures; direct federal payments (direct-pay tax incentives) are needed to put co-ops on equal footing with for-profit utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct-pay incentives would allow co-ops and their member systems to directly build or procure renewable generation and reap benefits without resorting to third-party ownership models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinance RUS loans without prepayment penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow electric cooperatives to refinance federal Rural Utilities Service (RUS) loans at lower interest rates without costly prepayment penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed Flexible Financing for Rural America Act would permit refinancing and could save an average co-op with typical RUS debt about $2 million per year in interest at current rates; increases financial flexibility and long-term stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide financing programs to support voluntary energy transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer targeted funding programs (e.g., USDA voluntary energy transition program) to help co-ops defray costs of voluntarily retiring coal plants or investing in renewable energy and other low-carbon technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants/loans/programs should help manage transition costs and reduce burdens on member-owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for major transmission expansion to support electrification
rubrics_metrics.description: Electrifying other sectors will require a substantial expansion of the transmission grid (e.g., a three-fold expansion) and significantly more electricity supply by midcentury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission capacity and deployment timelines must be accounted for when setting decarbonization goals; transmission upgrades are time-consuming and costly and affect the feasibility of rapid decarbonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline federal permitting and NEPA processes for transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear guidance and analysis timeframes for NEPA compliance and encourage categorical exclusions for projects with minimal impact to reduce excessive permitting delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal NEPA reviews can take years in contrast to state siting processes that take months; coordinated interagency approaches and clearer timeframes will reduce delays and costs for transmission development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory protections for lawful utility activities (wildlife/conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide regulatory protections for utilities engaging in lawful activities (such as power transmission) when those activities implicate endangered species or migratory bird regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address permitting/mitigation liability to avoid chilling transmission development due to potential compliance challenges under statutes like the Endangered Species Act or Migratory Bird Treaty Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allocation for transmission development commensurate with benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the costs of transmission development are borne by users commensurate to the benefits from development of renewable energy projects and the transmission connecting the projects to those areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should align costs with beneficiaries to avoid undue burdens on co-op members or local consumers when transmission primarily serves distant renewable projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weatherization and winterization of generation and gas infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Weatherize generation facilities and critical natural gas infrastructure to improve resiliency during extreme weather events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections and enhanced weatherization measures (e.g., winterization requirements imposed by legislature/PUC) are necessary; mapping critical gas infrastructure and requiring weatherization of designated assets increases system resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate across agencies and between gas and electric sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalize interagency frameworks and industry coordination to ensure effective communication and operational collaboration during emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms like councils including oil and gas representatives, PUCs, ERCOT, and regulators facilitate communication during events and ensure the electricity supply chain operates reliably; co-ops need a seat at the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exposing consumers to excessive retail-choice rate indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect consumers from retail providers indexing rates to extreme wholesale prices and increase accountability standards for retail choice providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative and regulatory actions (e.g., prohibitions on extreme indexing, lowering maximum wholesale price caps) can prevent consumer bill shocks observed during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in smart grid technologies and modernized substations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy smart grid technologies and modernize substations to provide more field data and improve operational responsiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smart technologies also act as catalysts for broadband and telecommunications in rural areas; investments lower member funding needs by improving efficiency and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate supply-chain and logistics challenges via planning and phased delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan projects and coordinate with developers to phase large jobs to allow staggered delivery of essential parts and components amid prolonged lead times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies include projecting multi-month demand, ordering staggered deliveries, using refurbished equipment, and increasing inventory reserves to avoid stockouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer protection measures during crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt measures such as suspending late fees and disconnections, relaxing deposit requirements, offering deferred payment plans, and delaying planned rate increases to protect consumers after extraordinary events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures soften the short-term economic impact on members following events like major outages or price shocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature retirement of baseload generation without system studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies should not incentivize early retirements of coal and gas resources without considering impacts on reliability, system costs, and the need for replacement resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses (e.g., MIT study) indicate gas and coal may still be necessary to 2030 under common scenarios; policymakers must consider who bears transition costs and impacts on vulnerable households and industrial competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure technology and transmission readiness before aggressive decarbonization mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mandate near-term targets (e.g., 100% carbon-free by 2035) unless generation, storage technologies and transmission infrastructure are sufficiently mature and deployable at required scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize practical constraints: pace of technology development, deployment rates, transmission upgrade timelines, and capital costs; balance aspiration with realism to avoid undermining reliability or affordability.
